subject: Cross-border hosting readiness & recommended next steps
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Prashant Kumar <prashant.kumar@ozonhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Cross-border hosting readiness & recommended next steps

Hi Prashant — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment on Ozon's residency and hosting constraints.

Key points from the call:
- Primary requirement: EU residency for all PHI-derived inference requests for EU customers.
- Secondary use case: APAC pilots (Singapore) for a user subset later in the year — APAC residency will be a hard requirement for those pilot datasets.
- Performance: sub-250ms 95th percentile token latency for chat workloads is the target for Ozon's clinician UI.
- Volume estimate: steady-state 20 QPS with peak bursts to 60 QPS during business hours.

Immediate qualification implications:
1) Hosted API (Redwood-hosted EU region): satisfies EU residency for production EU traffic and gives fastest path for demos. However, cross-region access from APAC users will route to EU unless APAC hosting is enabled — that could increase latency.
2) Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs in EU): meets residency + provides predictable throughput for the 20–60 QPS profile. It simplifies tail-latency guarantees and lets you pin a model variant.
3) Private VPC (customer-managed VPC or on-prem): required if Ozon needs on-prem control of keys or strict network egress policies. Also the only path to keep APAC pilot traffic within APAC if Ozon elects a separate APAC VPC.

My recommendation (short-term vs long-term):
- Short-term (0–3 months): spin up Redwood-hosted EU proof-of-concept for EU users to validate latency and accuracy. This lets you start evaluation while we work procurement.
- Mid-term (3–6 months): provision Dedicated capacity in the EU for production cutover if procurement commits allow. Provides SLAs and predictable unit costs.
- Parallel (6+ months): evaluate Private VPC for APAC residency requirement for the pilot — we can run an APAC VPC or on-prem node depending on your KMS constraints.

Action items I propose for this week:
- Ozon: share the redlined security questionnaire and the KMS requirements (Prashant) — I have attached our hosted_vs_vpc_matrix and the questionnaire you requested.
- Redwood: Ben to validate GPU sizing for 60 QPS peaks and provide Dedicated capacity estimate; Monica to draft a VPC onboarding checklist for APAC.

If that looks right I can convert this into a brief mutual action plan and a timeline.

Thanks — Hannah

--
Hannah Schmitt

From: Prashant Kumar <prashant.kumar@ozonhealth.com>

Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 10:03:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Cross-border hosting readiness & recommended next steps

Hannah — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from Ozon's side: 

- The EU residency constraint is mandatory for any traffic touching EU patient metadata. For the APAC pilot we need an explicit confirmation that traffic from Singapore can be kept in APAC (no EU egress). That's a blocker for us if we want to run pilots in Q4.
- KMS: we prefer customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key). If Private VPC is required for BYOK, we need an estimate of integration effort and downtime risk.
- Latency: sub-250ms is a stretch for APAC if traffic routes to EU; we need numbers for estimated p95 from Singapore to EU-hosted endpoint.

Can you have Ben share GPU sizing + a rough p95 latency estimate for Singapore->EU hosted path? Also please include any routing fallback options in case Dedicated capacity in EU becomes saturated.

I'll upload our redlines to the questionnaire by EOD.

Regards,
Prashant
Director of Platform Engineering, Ozon Health
prashant.kumar@ozonhealth.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Prashant Kumar <prashant.kumar@ozonhealth.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 13:28:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Cross-border hosting readiness & recommended next steps

Hi Prashant — quick technical inputs attached. Highlights: 

- For the chat workload you described (context lengths ~1.5k tokens, model medium-8b quantized), we estimate:
  * Hosted EU p95 (EU clients): ~120–180ms server-side tokens (network excluded).
  * Singapore -> EU-hosted p95 network + server: ~280–420ms depending on public internet path; with a dedicated interconnect (partner cloud), we can target ~210–300ms.
- Dedicated capacity sizing: for steady 20 QPS / peak 60 QPS bursts we recommend a pool of 4x0.5s latency-optimized GPU nodes (N model), with auto-burst to two extra nodes for a 10–14 day ramp test. Cost estimate included in the matrix.
- Routing fallbacks: Redwood can configure policy-based routing so APAC-origin traffic hits an APAC-hosted compatible model variant (lower-size) if EU capacity is saturated. That keeps service online but may affect model quality slightly — we can add threshold-based automatic fallback rules.

Attachments: hosted_vs_vpc_matrix.pdf (cost/sizing matrix), hosting_network-latency-estimates.csv, security-questionnaire-ozon.xlsx

I'll loop in Infra if you want a synchronous deep dive on interconnect options.

-ben

--
Ben Carter

Perfect — thanks Prashant and Ben. Short next-step plan I will track: 

1) Prashant: drop redlines into the security-questionnaire-ozon.xlsx by EOD today (you mentioned that in the call).
2) Ben: finalize Dedicated capacity estimate and a short playbook for APAC fallback rules (we want the exact thresholds and behavior documented).
3) Monica: prepare a VPC onboarding checklist for an APAC pilot (BYOK steps + expected lead times).
4) Hannah: I will draft a 3-month mutual action plan and attach the matrix + the latency estimate in HubSpot; propose a pilot kickoff week for early Oct.

If we can get the questionnaire back this week and the Dedicated estimate by next Tue 7/6, we can put procurement and legal on a path for a late Q3 decision.

Thanks — I'll send the MAP doc in a separate email after I sync with Solutions.

Best,
Hannah
